name: Height is law

lead: "Height is law" is a slogan from looksmaxxing forums holding that height is the most important single physical trait, often placed above face. It frames height as the feature that most shapes how others perceive a man, and it is the stated reason many people turn to height-adding options.

In forums, believers cite personal experience: shorter men with good faces who struggle, and taller men with average faces who do well. Others reply with counterexamples of tall men without success. Published research does link height with occupational and perceived-status outcomes in some studies, though effects vary by sex and context.

paras: As a framework, it directs attention to practical height options: shoe lifts and insoles, posture and standing-height improvements, adolescent growth optimisation, and surgical limb lengthening. Followers also compare themselves in height tiers.

The framework itself has no physical risk, but community members describe distress when they feel short, and the most extreme height-adding route, limb lengthening, is major surgery with its own risks.

angle.text: The belief points practitioners toward concrete height options such as lifts, posture and standing-height work, and surgical lengthening. It acts as a prioritisation framework more than a technique.

lead: "Height is law" (also written "heightlaw") is a slogan in looksmaxxing communities asserting that height is the dominant physical trait for attractiveness and social standing, sometimes ranked above facial features. Followers use it to justify putting height first when deciding what to work on, from shoe lifts to growth-focused routines and, in some cases, limb-lengthening surgery.[1]

Threads on looksmax.org show the belief in practice: one poster of 5 feet 11 inches describes feeling short and says taller friends with less attractive faces have more dating success, while others in the same thread report being taller than most people yet still being out-heighted by the occasional taller man.[1] Counterclaims also appear, such as tall users who report little romantic interest.

Research on height and life outcomes exists in economics and psychology. A review of the literature links height with occupational success in several studies, although sex and socioeconomic status may explain part of the association.[2]

paras: The phrase states that height carries decisive weight in how men are judged, often in contrast to the face-first emphasis of the PSL scale tradition. Posters usually acknowledge that face matters, but argue that being well below average height cannot be offset by facial attractiveness.[1]

Proponents report anecdotes about dating outcomes and being asked about height on apps, with some saying they state a taller height to avoid being filtered out.[1] Others argue height is a proxy for health and good development, a view also found in evolutionary accounts of mate preference.[3]
Critics within the forums point to tall users with little success and attribute outcomes to personality or social skills.[1]

Research links body height with occupational success and earnings in several studies, including work by Judge and Cable (2004) and Heineck (2005), though some of the association may reflect sex and socioeconomic status, and height is largely unrelated to job performance in most fields.[2] A discussion of the height-intelligence correlation notes that people may prefer partners high in both traits, since each is associated with fitness.[3]

Height is a staple of community tier lists and threads, and "height is law" is the shorthand used when advising on shoe lifts, growth, or limb lengthening. The related slang includes being "height mogged" by a taller person.[1]
No studies found on the slogan itself. Related published research on height and occupational outcomes is summarised above.[2]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the phrase appears in threads comparing height with face and in personal accounts of dating outcomes.[1]
